title: Enhanced Box Score: Cardinals 3, Cubs 2 - July 29, 2026 - NewsBreak
text:
By Michael Cerami ,
1 hours ago Well, that’s a “rip up the entire postgame write-up and pretend you weren’t stomping on the Cardinals’ grave” ending if I ever had one.
Tonight, in extra innings, despite PCA’s heroics in the top half of the 10th, the Cubs lost to the Cardinals 3-2. Having already used Jacob Webb and Caleb Thielbar to get to extra innings, Trent Thornton was the man on the mound when Jordan Walker came around to score from first base on Ivan Herrera’s walk-off double. And that was that.
Probably a good time to remind Jed Hoyer that STARTING pitching isn’t the only type of pitching the Cubs need to acquire at the deadline. Even if Daniel Palencia (and maybe Hunter Harvey, Ben Brown, and eventually Justin Steele, Colin Rea, and Javier Assad could join that group). Sigh. With a win tonight, the Cubs would’ve moved to a season-high 16-games over .500. I was looking forward to that.
Alas.
Let’s talk a little more about the game.
As crazy as it would’ve sounded in May, right now, it’s not easy to shut down this Cubs offense the way Dustin May (5.0 IP, 1H, 2BB, 3K) and the Cardinals bullpen did in regulation. But it happened. Through the first nine innings, the Cubs managed just ONE hit and six walks, while plating none. Pete Crow-Armstrong, who pimped the HELL out of it, gave the Cubs a 2-run lead on his go-ahead home run in the 10th, but that’s all the Cubs could muster. And it wasn’t enough.
For just a moment, I was so enjoying how mad all the fans in the tarps off section of Busch (probably) were.
In any case, our Ankin Law “Making it Personal” Player of the Game tonight is Matthew Boyd, who has returned to the Cubs from the Injured List like a knight in shining armor.
The Cubs veteran lefty and de facto ace tossed another gem, scattering just four hits and two walks against five strikeouts over seven scoreless innings in St. Louis. He found his way into a little bit of trouble in the fifth and sixth, but got out of both jams and ended with a 1-2-3 final appearance in the seventh.
Speaking of that trouble, early on, it looked like Boyd was going to be efficient enough to go even further tonight. He had cruised through 4.2 innings at just 45 pitches, but then hit a batter, walked a batter, and took JJ Wetherholt to a full count in a frustratingly long 10-pitch at-bat before getting him to ground out and end the inning.
If one or two of those at-bats go differently, he might’ve gone at least eight tonight, which may have pushed Jacob Webb and Caleb Thielbar each back an inning. Then, who knows. Butterfly wings and all that, but that’s on my mind.
But seriously, Boyd is on a great run, and you just have to pray he stays healthy the rest of the season. Because the way he’s throwing it right now, at least in terms of results, is looking like a playoff-caliber starter.
